clue.text: Booth is keen to help knock out variation

indicators.note: a variation is a changed version, so the letters before it are to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
KO is the boxing abbreviation for a knockout

explanation.surface: Someone at a stall or booth is eager to help with a boxing variation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like the link after 'Booth', but it is part of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone kiosk is the British name for a public phone box, a small enclosed booth.

clue.text: See 6
See 6
Contrition demands about 1-10 coins

indicators.note: about means around, so the coins word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: pence are British coins
1 as the Roman numeral I, then 10 written out as a word

explanation.surface: Remorse calls for a payment of a handful of coins, as in a fine.
explanation.walkthrough: '1-10' looks like a cross-reference to other clues, but it just gives I and TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Penitence is sorrow and regret for wrongdoing, the same feeling as contrition.

clue.text: What stops one making Close bat?

indicators.note: making suggests the next words are the raw material from which something new is built

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket question: what prevents a batter from being a close one?
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle is a barrier or hindrance, anything that blocks progress or halts a person.

clue.text: 4 to listener makes spike get bigger

parts.note: an ear is the spike of a cereal plant holding the grain
to wax is to grow, as the moon does

explanation.surface: Something odd: a spike that grows larger in a hearer's presence.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 is OBSTACLE, so the definition is an obstacle to hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Earwax builds up in the canal of the ear and can block sound, a barrier to hearing.

clue.text: Funny thing afoot — shy vernal youths go contemplating girls: Thus (in catalectic trochees) poem by 19 unfurls

definitions.text: Funny thing afoot — shy vernal youths go contemplating girls: Thus (in catalectic trochees) poem by 19 unfurls

parts.words: Funny thing afoot — shy vernal youths go contemplating girls
parts.note: surface reading: a comic observation about bashful young men in springtime eyeing up girls

parts.words: Thus (in catalectic trochees) poem by 19 unfurls
parts.note: setter's reading: the same idea as it is put in a famous line of verse by the poet at 19, written in trochaic metre with a short final foot

annotation.spelling: IN THE SPRING A YOUNG MAN'S FANCY LIGHTLY TURNS TO THOUGHTS OF LOVE

explanation.surface: A wry remark about shy young men thinking of girls in spring, then a nod to how a poet phrased it.
explanation.walkthrough: The line comes from Tennyson's Locksley Hall, whose long lines are trochaic with the last foot cut short, which is what catalectic means.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted line says exactly that young men's minds turn to romance when the season changes to spring.

clue.text: See 6
See 6
Wildly erring as chasing round, needing this — could be personal

definitions.note: points to the phrase personal organiser

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: doing something wildly means doing it out of control, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
positional: a pursuer comes behind, so the jumbled letters follow the round one

explanation.surface: Someone making wild mistakes while running round in circles needs help to get their life in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chasing' places the jumbled letters after O.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal organiser is a diary or electronic device for keeping appointments and contacts in order.

clue.text: Main body in government or society

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of government, all of or and the start of society

explanation.surface: A political remark about the central body of a government or of society.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, the main part without head or limbs.

clue.text: Leave bird, understood?

parts.note: to go is to leave
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: An instruction to leave a bird alone, followed by a check that it was heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking whether someone has grasped something is the colloquial question of comprehension.

clue.text: Greek leader soon holds willing number

indicators.note: something that holds another thing has it inside it

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon
to be game is to be willing
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A Greek party boss will shortly take on a willing number of followers.
explanation.walkthrough: The willing word and the number join first, then sit after the first letter of the soon word.
explanation.definitionFit: Agamemnon was king of Mycenae and commander of the Greek armies at Troy in Homer's epic.

clue.text: Vibrating outside line in tiresome style

indicators.note: outside says the first word goes around the second

parts.note: tingly describes a vibrating, prickling sensation
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Something shaking around a line is getting tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: Line as railway, abbreviated RY, is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying means tiresome or annoying, so the adverb describes acting in a wearisome manner.

clue.text: Take weapons from girl and take into boy

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name

indicators.note: putting something into a word places it inside that word

parts.note: Sam is a boy's name
R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A disarming plan: grab weapons from a girl and hand them to a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: R for 'take' comes from the Latin recipe heading old prescriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarm someone is to strip them of their arms, removing their weapons.

clue.text: No charge for accommodation for Yeats?

definitions.text: No charge for accommodation for Yeats?

parts.note: surface reading: lodging offered without payment
setter's reading: a place celebrated in a poem by Yeats, whose name sounds like a sign saying the pub costs nothing

explanation.surface: Free lodging offered to the Irish poet Yeats.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as INN IS FREE, the name of Yeats's lake isle reads as a notice of free lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lake Isle of Innisfree is one of Yeats's best-known poems, about an island in Lough Gill.

clue.text: Fellow at location of eruption?

parts.note: he is a male person, a fellow
taken as written
a spot is a place or location

explanation.surface: A man stands at the site where a volcano erupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eruption' suggests a volcano, but here it means a skin eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: A heat spot is a small red blemish on the skin caused by heat, a minor skin eruption.

clue.text: Release from striking by permit

parts.note: workers on strike are out
to let is to permit
places the next piece beside the first

explanation.surface: Someone is set free from a strike by official permission.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlet is a means of release or escape, as for feelings or water.

clue.text: See 6
Poet and boxer Benn not initially included

indicators.note: something included is held inside another word

parts.note: Mike Tyson, the heavyweight boxing champion

indicators.note: not initially says the first letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Nigel Benn, another boxer, losing his first letter

explanation.surface: A list pairing a poet with the British boxer Nigel Benn, who was not at first included.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was a Victorian Poet Laureate, author of In Memoriam and Locksley Hall.

clue.text: New as new as new city

indicators.note: making something new means rebuilding it, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tongue-twister repeating the word new as if describing a brand-new city.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'new' hides which one signals the rearrangement. Swansea, in Wales, was granted city status only in 1969.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a Welsh city that gained city status relatively recently, in 1969.

clue.text: Heard pair preserve bird

indicators.note: heard means the next word counts by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a pair is two
to can food is to preserve it in tins

explanation.surface: A couple are overheard keeping a bird alive or preserved.
explanation.definitionFit: The toucan is a tropical American bird known for its enormous brightly coloured bill.

clue.text: Bird needs a fight to have fun

parts.note: the lark is a songbird
taken as written
a bout is a boxing or wrestling match

explanation.surface: A bird must pick a fight just to enjoy itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To lark about is to fool around and play, behaving mischievously for amusement.

clue.text: Prize for one in chancery?

parts.note: a means one
a ward in chancery is a minor under the protection of the court

explanation.surface: A legal puzzle: a reward given to someone in the Chancery court.
explanation.walkthrough: Chancery is the division of the English High Court that handled wards, children under its guardianship.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a prize or honour given in recognition of achievement.

clue.text: Administration taking notes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the employees who run an organisation
second meaning: the five lines on which music is written

explanation.surface: Office workers busy writing down minutes at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking notes' suggests secretaries; here it describes what holds written music.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the people employed by an organisation and the set of musical lines, also called a stave.

clue.text: V is for Volunteers in prospect

parts.note: taken as written
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
means the next piece follows

explanation.surface: An alphabet primer line: V stands for Volunteers, perhaps a recruiting outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a view or outlook, and a prospect in the old sense is a wide view of scenery.

clue.text: Posh gear for prisoner outside a capital

indicators.note: outside says the prisoner word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a con is a convict
taken as written
Paris is the capital of France

explanation.surface: Smart clothes are being sent to a convict held in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A caparison is an ornamental cloth covering for a horse, and more loosely any rich finery.

clue.text: Left like godmother at christening?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: stuck with a responsibility others have abandoned
second meaning, playfully literal: cradling the infant at the font

explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a direction or a political wing; here it means abandoned with a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being saddled with responsibility, while literally a godmother may carry the infant during the ceremony.
